head: 22697f2a41f9b7387daf436e6672f204e51ba4b0
classification_reasons: Security/authorization control on sdlc.yaml's risk_list item 'auth', explicitly risk-accepted by the owner (status.yaml risk_accepted: [auth]) rather than closed by a tight, no-concern spec.

Blast radius is the guardrail-protection mechanism itself (plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py), registered on every Bash/PowerShell tool call in every phase, in CI and by hand (plugin/hooks/hooks.json), plus a sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite rewrite in plugin/ci/run_phase.py/settings.ci.json that every CI phase job reads.
The code is new (985 lines) with its own dedicated parser/tokenizer; it is not code the pre-existing test suite already covered before this change.
attempted: Intent: compared this round's diff against intent.md's proposed outcome ('no instance of this authz weakness remains'). This round closes the two concrete bypasses (git global-option-before-verb, inner-shell flag-before-'-c') that the prior two adversarial-review rounds (escalated at 08f5e65/7bc5ef2, upheld by the panel at commit 7bc5ef2) found still open in the previous HEAD.

Spec and plan: re-read spec.md Requirements/Design and plan.md Files-that-change/Order-of-work; the file list in the diff (plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py, hooks.json, plugin/ci/run_phase.py, settings.ci.json, tests/test_hooks.py, tests/test_ci.py, tests/test_evals.py, docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, the two .claude-plugin manifests) matches plan.md's 'Files that change' list exactly, no extra or missing file. One disclosed, non-blocking plan deviation found: plan.md's Order of work step 1 says the shell_guard import in tests/test_hooks.py should be 'inside the test functions, never at module top-level, so a failure in the new tests cannot abort collection of the rest of the file'; fix-response.md round 5 item 21 discloses this was left at module scope from an earlier round (a test-isolation robustness nit, not a correctness defect; every shell_guard test in the file currently passes with it at module scope).

Proof: independently re-traced, by hand, the exact two repro commands the prior two escalations used, directly against this HEAD's plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py source (not against any runner/claude-*.json/run-*.json record, and not by citing the gate's own deterministic result): `git -c core.fileMode=false rm CLAUDE.md` -> _git_global_scan correctly skips the '-c <value>' pair (name=='-c' is distinct from name=='-C' by case) and lands verb_index on 'rm', which now yields the candidate 'CLAUDE.md' and is denied (traced the actual index arithmetic in _git_global_scan/_part_targets, not just read the comment). `bash --norc -c 'echo x > CLAUDE.md'` -> _inner_shell_command now scans past any flag token ('--norc' starts with '-', so it is skipped) to find the adjacent '-c' and recurses into 'echo x > CLAUDE.md', whose '>' redirection now yields 'CLAUDE.md' and is denied. Both traces confirm the fix, independent of the tests. New tests test_shell_guard_sees_the_git_verb_after_a_global_option and test_shell_write_targets_sees_through_a_flag_before_the_inner_shell_s_c_token assert exactly these repro commands. No committed test.log/build.log/lint.log or a verifier.md scoped to this HEAD exist yet (the only verifier.md present is explicitly scoped to an earlier, already-superseded commit, 3a90bd0's git -C chain-leak fix, not to this round's 21-item fix) -- this round's own fix-response.md explicitly discloses the writer could not run the full suite in-session (an unrelated sandboxed-.env-fixture failure cascading through most test files that do not touch shell_guard.py) and self-reports only a partial in-session run; I did not treat that self-report as proof and relied on my own trace instead, per the instruction to judge the diff and the artifacts rather than cite the author's claim or any runner record.

Blast radius: read plugin/hooks/hooks.json's registration (one Bash|PowerShell matcher, timeout 30, --plugin-root wired) and plugin/ci/run_phase.py's ci_settings_file/_deny_write_entries changes; confirmed decide() now short-circuits to allow() before any config/branch/test-lock lookup when shell_write_targets finds no candidate at all (round 4 item 18), closing the fail-closed-on-unreadable-config risk for a plain 'git status' that the previous round's design did not have.

Policies: security-baseline rule 1 (authorization must not depend on which route reaches the target) is the rule this whole change exists to satisfy; spot-checked that none of the new test lines contain the security-baseline scanner's literal DANGEROUS patterns (eval(, exec(, shell=True) as source text, matching spec.md Acceptance's instruction to avoid those literals.

Tests: read the new ancestor-directory check (_protected_roots/_is_ancestor_of_protected) and traced it denies 'git rm -r -q .claude' and a recursive delete of an ancestor of a protected_paths entry (item 3); traced the '>&WORD' vs '>&2'/'2>&1' fd-dup distinction (item 12) and the subshell/lone-'&'/assignment-prefix tokenizer changes (item 9) by hand against their stated repro commands; found each produces the claimed, correct result. Did not find a case among those sampled where the bug described by the owner's review would still pass the new tests.

Cross-checked this verdict is independent of the gate's own deterministic checks (did not run gate/cli.py check, checks.py or any skill's check.py) and did not cite or rely on any claude-*.json/run-*.json/gate-c.json runner record (the committed gate-c.json/status.yaml predate this HEAD and reflect the prior round's escalate, which the gate will re-run and overwrite after this verdict).
